answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory cards, randomly select players + 1 face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly select one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: select number of players + 1 Factory cards; one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories; choose one structure bonus tile. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: Place each character at its home base; place two workers on the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; place four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; put six stars by the faction emblem; put six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with black squares; structures in their matching Player Mat boxes; recruits in the bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement. Starting power and combat-card draw come from the Faction Mat. Starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards come from the Player Mat.
answers.evidence: Setup pieces table and step 3: Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins and objectives.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action. Rusviet may repeat a section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. If both actions are taken, top must precede bottom; top-row gains may pay the bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before acting, then take as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired; the Player Mat and upgrades determine the costs and benefits.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: may take either, both, or neither but must move token; bottom first is not allowed; pay full cost, then choose as much or as little benefit.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units cannot use your structure's abilities; you keep the abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. You may pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone controls it and resources; enemy units do not gain your structure abilities; spend resources from any currently controlled territories.

answers.answer: No. A normal Move can move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. All units can pick up, carry and drop any number of resources. Only mechs can carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker's transport does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: move up to two different units; cannot use both selections to move same unit twice. All units carry resources; only mechs carry workers; carried movement does not count as worker's own movement.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero. Having too little or zero popularity does not stop their retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers, and workers cannot independently enter or leave territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Move rules: entering enemy workers only causes immediate retreat and one popularity lost per worker, down to zero; workers cannot independently enter or move into/out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve combats before the following bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Combat: after all units finish a Move action, fights occur before any subsequent bottom action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Move rules restrict workers entering or leaving enemy character/mech-controlled territory alone.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gains either two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat draw deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gains either any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Put traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster: pay $1, gain two power OR one combat card; empty deck reshuffle rule. Trade: pay $1, choose two resources or one popularity; resources placed on controlled territory containing a worker; cannot trade for resources if all workers at home.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost in full, including power, popularity and/or coins, before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers never return to the Player Mat, and exposing new costs changes only future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: pay every exposed cost in full before production; each worker in selected territories produces; take new workers from Player Mat left to right after payment; may decline; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; it moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake, and its newly uncovered ability applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Costs vary with the mat and upgrades. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Upgrade and Deploy: pay exposed mat costs in oil/metal; stated effects and placement restrictions. Bottom-row actions: may still pay after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total can occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives its bonus production only while you control its territory; an enemy there can remove your control, so the Mill cannot produce then. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your unit movement even while an enemy occupies its territory. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: placement, one structure limit, no lakes/home bases, structures cannot be moved or destroyed. Mill only while controlled; Mine remains a personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Put the recruit token from any bottom-row section into any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat permanently, and immediately gain that chosen space's two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle exposed where you removed the recruit. When you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes the corresponding bottom action, resolve the active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor, stopping if a sixth star ends play. In a two-player game the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: permanent placement and one-time choices; circle uncovered determines ongoing bonus; active player then left then right; two-player opponent once.

answers.answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly chooses dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power. Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. Reveal simultaneously, total dial plus card values, and attacker wins ties. If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first and defender second. Both deduct their selected dial power from their Power Track and discard played cards face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4: simultaneous secret dial selection, optional cards per character/mech, People's Army extra card, simultaneous reveal and tie rule, abilities order, and payment.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources. Losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat (including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake); a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's combat exception. A non-Saxony winner with zero or one combat star places one, and with two places none; Saxony places a star after each victory while it has star tokens. You may keep fighting at the limit. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6: control, retreat/resources, combat stars, popularity loss and losing-card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; if contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token remains. Only a character triggers it. Put all gained resources, workers, mechs, and structures on the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action cost, and receive no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only character triggers; after Move and all combats; token stays if contested entry lost; gains go to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat bonuses.

answers.answer: Every player's character must choose one available Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if necessary; this is not just the first player to visit. Each player gets one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. It acts as a fifth section with optional top then bottom, subject to the normal no-repeat rule except Rusviet. Similar Factory actions do not grant corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom Move action moves one unit up to two territories within that action, or up to three for a character/mech with Speed, subject to Mine access and normal stop restrictions.
answers.evidence: Factory: every character picks on first finish of Move there; one permanent card; fifth section; no mat/recruit/building bonuses; bottom Move distance and Speed.

answers.answer: You may reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, and must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal; you may wait to reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the objective deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, all requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom, Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars normally), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars cannot be lost, and another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists every star goal, permanence, no blocking, and sixth-star ending.

answers.answer: For a sixth star from a bottom-row action, first collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. Resolve recruit bonuses active player first, then left, then right, checking for a sixth star after each; if one ends the game, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: bottom action collection order, neighbor recruit sequence, and pending-battle movement rollback.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete resource pair. Five stars add $20. Four normal controlled territories plus the Factory count as seven, adding $21. Thirteen resources make six complete pairs, adding $12; total added to held coins is $53. Add the selected structure bonus from your structures even if enemies control their territories. Victory goes by total coins, then workers + mechs + structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: popularity 7–12 rates; Factory is three counts; complete pairs rounded down; structures qualify despite enemy control; listed tiebreakers.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory. Normally you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: home base is not a territory; entry exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if necessary.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources paragraph says workers are not resources and resource tokens have no supply limit.

answers.answer: Any unit can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; only mechs can carry your workers, and never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, so the added step can be before or after it. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: all units carry resources, mechs carry workers; Speed and tunnel jump step rules; stops override Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter territory held only by an enemy structure and take control without combat. Printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move rules: entry into enemy-structure-only territory; all printed tunnels adjacent for any unit.

answers.answer: You may not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. The token must move from the section used last turn, so after using Move you choose a different section.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: pay costs in full, never part; if unable to afford any action, move token to a different section and take neither.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are future matching top-action bonuses from the uncovered structure benefits. You keep your structure abilities even without control of the territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
answers.evidence: Build structure effects; control rules say abilities remain without control except Mill production, and enemy units do not gain abilities.

answers.answer: Riverwalk destinations for character/mechs are Rusviet: farms and villages; Crimea: farms and tundra; Nordic: forests and mountains; Polania: villages and mountains; Saxony: forests and mountains. These destinations apply to character/mechs. Nordic Swim lets workers cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs or mechs generally.
answers.evidence: Faction table identifies Riverwalk destinations; Nordic Swim description says workers alone, not lakes, and no help to character/mechs.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
answers.evidence: Unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township explicitly specify character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery is different: before combat you may pay one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers permit three combat cards total: the normal one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total from People's Army when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight; combat still requires a character or mech.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: two mechs and three workers allow three cards; combat rules require character/mech and workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare allows character/mechs to move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It does not allow entry to an active opponent home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description explicitly states destinations and excludes active opponent bases.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of the card's value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea starting Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake; Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake, but Polania has no adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off, and a carrier cannot leave workers or resources behind on a lake. Both allow lake combat; neither permits building or deploying on lakes.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy and Polania Submerge descriptions; lake movement edge-case paragraph.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description states its combat condition and excludes loss for undefended workers.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. Resolve each option in turn; the first gain may pay the second option's cost. The summary does not say Polania draws or uses two encounter cards; it specifies up to two options on one card.
answers.evidence: Meander: up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost.

answers.answer: In a Factory bottom Move, a character entering an encounter-token territory stops and cannot continue moving that turn. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there; the encounter does not happen before combats finish.
answers.evidence: Encounter rules say character stops; after whole Move action and all combats; same rules apply during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total value when asked. Combat-card hand count is public, though during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents remain secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table.

answers.answer: Informal agreements are unenforceable, and coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (with coin deal/alliances forbidden in tournament play). Negotiation cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units; combat must be fought after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section states exchange, enforceability and initiated combat rules.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6, score $3 per star, $2 per territory count, and $1 per complete resource pair; at 7–12, $4, $3, and $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, and $3. Controlled lakes count as territories; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a single leftover resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table and territory/resource counting paragraphs.

answers.answer: For adjacent-feature tiles, count unique printed tunnel territories (not Mines), unique lakes, or unique printed encounter locations (even when tokens have been removed); count each feature once across all structures. The summary does not specify a special exception for duplicate adjacency beyond uniqueness. Rivers do not break adjacency. For 1 feature pay $2; 2–3 pay $4; 4–5 pay $6; tunnels pay $9 at 6, while lakes and encounters pay $9 at 6–7. Zero scores $0.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table gives qualifying unique features and payout bands; rivers do not break adjacency.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6. For structures in a row, count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9. For structures on farms/tundras, count combined qualifying structures; 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table rows for structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: Placing a popularity star is permanent, but it does not protect current popularity or its final-scoring tier: current popularity at game end determines scoring. Two factions may both place stars for the same achievement because other players' stars never block a goal.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: stars permanent even if popularity later drops; current popularity determines final scoring; other players' stars never block a goal.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seat order matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can be triggered by the active player and immediate left/right neighbors, in active-then-left-then-right order.
answers.evidence: Setup: random mats and faction seating order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left/right neighbors trigger and sequence.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move rules define river and lake; lake-capable unit entry from any surrounding adjoining land territory.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounter procedure: show card to all players, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text; options need not all be read.

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin while current player decides which bottom-row item to gain after starting a noninteractive bottom-row action.

answers.answer: No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within a turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's repeat ability waives only the restriction on repeating a section used last turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure explicitly limits chosen top and bottom actions to once within the turn, including Rusviet.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units with the normal, unupgraded Move top action.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; workers produced from a village come from the mat left to right. The summary says retreating workers go to their home base, not back to the Player Mat.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to the Player Mat. Move/combat: retreating workers go to their home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Combat section: you may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching the two combat-star limit; a non-Saxony winner with two combat stars simply places no further combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat: non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places none; may still fight after limit.

answers.answer: No. A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose any option; unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. After paying the printed cost, it may take as little of the chosen benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: non-Meander must choose one affordable option; unaffordable options cannot be selected; may take as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No turn-order selection is specified: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose their dials, then reveal simultaneously after optional combat cards are selected.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose, then reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved; because the sixth star immediately ends play, you cannot delay or decline a star to avoid ending the game. An objective differs because you may wait to reveal a completed objective, but must meet all its requirements at the moment you reveal it.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved; sixth star ends immediately. Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal.

answers.answer: Normally, no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions; Nordic Swim allows only workers to cross rivers to land terrain and not lakes.
answers.evidence: Move rules: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities are exceptions.

answers.answer: No. Once placed on an open one-time recruit bonus on the Faction Mat, the recruit cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit is put permanently on any open one-time bonus and cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not trigger or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: While controlled, a Mill adds one bonus production territory to the normal Produce allowance: two normal territories become up to three, or an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill counts as one producing worker itself, even with no actual worker there; each actual worker at the Mill also produces normally, so Mill output is added rather than substituted.
answers.evidence: Produce Mill paragraph specifies extra territory, Mill's own output, actual workers' additional output, and allowance examples.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control it.
answers.evidence: Control definition: unit present, or your structure there with no enemy unit.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; Build—wood; Enlist—food.
